label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
**One star: good staff interface, but support has failed us badly**

Bridger Bend Community Library is a one-branch library with two full-time staff, a crew of volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. We signed a three-year, $14,200-a-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud in June and went live on October 19.

Since October 28, circulation has not worked normally. Checkouts run offline on a single laptop, and our holds queue was wiped, roughly 640 holds. One of our volunteers is writing checkouts on index cards. Last week a patron drove 40 minutes to pick up a large-print book he had on hold. We had no record of it, and he went home empty-handed. In a town this size, that kind of thing sticks.

Our support ticket has been open 12 days. We've had three replies, each saying the issue was "escalated to engineering." We have had no diagnosis, no timeline, and no workaround. During sales, we were promised a dedicated migration specialist. What we got was a shared inbox.

To be fair, the demo was accurate about one thing. The staff interface is better than our old system, and I think the product itself has promise. My complaint is with how Stackhouse handles a customer in trouble, especially a small one that can't absorb weeks of downtime.

I've been told someone from Stackhouse will call me this week. I'll update this review after we talk. If the problems are fixed, I'll gladly revisit my rating.

**For other directors considering Stackhouse:** get these in writing before you sign.
- Guaranteed support response and resolution times, with a named escalation contact
- What "dedicated migration specialist" means, and who it is
- A rollback or backup plan if go-live fails
- What remedy you get if the system is down during the contract

Ask the hard questions first. We wish we had.

*Bridger Bend Community Library*

---

I left the patron unnamed and left out the budget hearing, since mentioning it could read as leverage rather than a plain account. If you'd like it to run closer to 250 words, the contract detail and the last bullet list are the easiest places to trim. Update the "someone will call me" line once you know the person's name or title, since a named person is harder for them to walk back.
